title: 38-year-old with slowly progressive asymmetric parkinsonism and mild leg posturing

provenance.citation: Synthetic case written 2026-10-17 for Rare Disease Detective; not derived from any individual patient.

chief_complaint: "My right side has been slow and stiff for years, and my right foot cramps when I walk."
history_of_present_illness: Seven years of slowly progressive right-sided slowness and stiffness, beginning with smaller, slower handwriting and difficulty with fine tasks such as buttoning and using a computer mouse. A mild right-hand tremor appears when holding a phone or a cup; he has never noticed it with the hand resting in his lap. About six years ago he began to get cramping of the right foot with inversion and toe curling during long walks, usually after 20–30 minutes. When asked about time-of-day effects he says he 'hasn't paid attention' because he has been on levodopa for four years; before treatment he recalls being 'clumsier after work' but attributed it to tiredness. Sleep does not obviously help. No REM sleep behavior disorder symptoms per his partner, no anosmia, no constipation, no urinary symptoms, no orthostatic light-headedness. Started on levodopa by a previous neurologist 4 years ago with marked benefit within the first week; the dose has remained 100 mg TID since, with no wearing-off and no dyskinesia. If a dose is delayed by several hours the right foot cramp returns during walking. Seeking a second opinion because 'I was told it's young-onset Parkinson's but it hasn't progressed like they said it would.'

symptom_timeline.event: Right hand slowness, small handwriting, difficulty with buttons
Right foot cramping with inversion after 20–30 min of walking
Mild right-hand tremor when holding objects
Diagnosed young-onset PD; carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 TID started; marked improvement within one week
Follow-up with same neurologist: 'surprisingly stable'; no dose change
Stable on same dose; no motor fluctuations or dyskinesia; requests second opinion

movement_findings.observation: On medication: mild right-hand bradykinesia on finger tapping and hand opening, reduced speed without progressive amplitude decrement over 10 taps.
Mild right-hand postural tremor, 6–7 Hz, low amplitude; no rest tremor during distraction (serial sevens) or while walking.
On medication: normal gait with mildly reduced right arm swing; no foot posturing during a 10-minute corridor walk.
Handwriting sample: mild micrographia on the right without progressive shrinking along the line; no dystonic posturing of the hand while writing.
Facial expression and blink rate normal; speech normal in volume and articulation.

neurological_exam.tone: Mild right upper limb rigidity with activation, on medication
neurological_exam.other: Examined on medication, 2 hours after the morning dose (around 10 AM). Smell subjectively normal; no formal olfactory testing. No orthostatic drop in blood pressure. Pull test normal.

labs.note: Slit lamp and urine copper not performed

imaging.report: No structural abnormality. Basal ganglia normal in signal. No abnormal susceptibility. Impression: normal.

prior_trials.response: Marked improvement, sustained, no fluctuations or dyskinesia

family_history: Negative for movement disorders as far as the patient knows. Parents alive and well in their 60s. Not adopted.
social_history: Software engineer, works full time. Married, one child (age 3), developing normally. Non-smoker, drinks 2–3 beers per week, no recreational drugs. No toxin, solvent, manganese, or neuroleptic/antiemetic exposure.
prior_workup_and_opinions: Previous neurologist: young-onset Parkinson disease. No DAT imaging was performed. No genetic testing.
